comment: Lines 381–389 state the problem precisely: a government "can hold formal ownership of a system while lacking the practical ability to access its data, modify it, or move away from the supplier that runs it", and the architecture should place practical control with the public entity "through open standards, documented interfaces, data portability, and clear separation between the data a country owns and the systems that process it". The Ministry endorses this without reservation. The principle names no mechanism by which the separation is achieved. Documented interfaces and portability are necessary but operate after the fact: they describe how data is retrieved from a system that has already determined its structure. Separation is achieved when the structure of the data is defined and governed by the public authority independently of any system, so that a system can be replaced without the data being converted. That is what an open, vendor-neutral information model provides, and it is the concrete expression this principle currently lacks.

public.text: Lines 381–389 state the problem precisely: a government "can hold formal ownership of a system while lacking the practical ability to access its data, modify it, or move away from the supplier that runs it", and the architecture should place practical control with the public entity "through open standards, documented interfaces, data portability, and clear separation between the data a country owns and the systems that process it". The Ministry endorses this without reservation. The principle names no mechanism by which the separation is achieved. Documented interfaces and portability are necessary but operate after the fact: they describe how data is retrieved from a system that has already determined its structure. Separation is achieved when the structure of the data is defined and governed by the public authority independently of any system, so that a system can be replaced without the data being converted. That is what an open, vendor-neutral information model provides, and it is the concrete expression this principle currently lacks.
public.suggestedRevision: Add after line 389: "Separation of this kind is achieved most directly where the structure of the data, and not only its interfaces, is defined and governed by the public authority independently of the systems that process it. Where a country's clinical data conforms to an openly specified information model that it governs, a supplier's system can be replaced without the data being converted; where structure is determined by the system, portability guarantees access to data whose meaning still depends on the system that produced it."
